mechanisms.decisive_claim: After the rough high-tail reduction, the support size of every minimal bad event is bounded by a function only of L and maximum active degree, so event neighborhoods admit a sublogarithmic generic compression.
mechanisms.kill_test: RR.1 has fixed L, maximum active degree two, and arbitrarily large support-minimal path events.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Every residual bad active-incidence component has positive cycle rank, so deleting a sparse feedback set removes every failure polymer.
mechanisms.kill_test: RR.1 is a support-minimal bad component whose active-incidence graph is a tree path.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Every residual bad active-incidence tree contains a proper bad subrelation within a uniformly bounded radius, reducing alteration to bounded local witnesses.
mechanisms.kill_test: RR.1 is support-minimal and has arbitrarily large path diameter at fixed L and active degree two.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: A dependent alteration defined on complete connected prime-incidence components has total repair cost g(N) sum_n w_N(n)+o(N) for some g(N)=o(log N), uniformly over rough paths, fans, and their overlaps.
mechanisms.kill_test: Compute exact repair charge on disjoint and shared-boundary RR.1 path books; reject unless a symbolic cluster compression bounds every all-N overlap.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The prime support and factor complexity of the cofactor residue after a balanced top-prime fibre are bounded by a function of the top-fibre cardinality.
mechanisms.kill_test: RR.2 always has top-fibre cardinality two but transfers prod(B)/prod(A) with arbitrarily large independent numerator and denominator prime supports.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: For fixed roughness parameter L and bounded maximum active degree, successive largest-prime residue transfers terminate after a bounded number of steps independent of circuit support.
mechanisms.kill_test: Order RR.1 edge primes increasingly along an arbitrarily long path at fixed L and active degree two.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: If the two cofactors exposed at the top prime are coprime, their lower-prime states split into independent components and cannot carry the original imbalance jointly.
mechanisms.kill_test: In RR.2 the exposed cofactors X and Y are coprime, yet the lower singleton terms connect them into one support-minimal double-star relation.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: There is a noncircular owner map using the full ordered top-prime and cofactor residue state whose distinct owners have total cost g(N) sum_n w_N(n)+o(N), with g(N)=o(log N).
mechanisms.kill_test: Evaluate owner flow and reused-owner congestion on arbitrarily long RR.1 paths and overlapping RR.2 double-star books.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Every residual bad token state has positive active-incidence cycle rank, and each largest-prime transition strictly decreases this potential.
mechanisms.kill_test: RR.1 starts as a bad support-minimal tree with cycle rank zero.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Replacing a balanced top-prime pair by its two signed cofactors strictly decreases the number of residue tokens at every recursive step.
mechanisms.kill_test: On RR.1, stripping the largest path-edge prime replaces its two incident integers by two nontrivial cofactors, preserving token count while transferring the state to the next edge.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: A lower-prime admission decision that is safe at one finite prime prefix can be frozen forever without reserving future deletions, because later larger primes cannot create a new cross-prefix bad relation.
mechanisms.kill_test: RR.2 completes arbitrary unequal lower prime sets A,B by one later prime p into the minimal relation A union {p prod B} versus B union {p prod A}.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: A global multiscale potential combining cofactor height, component support, log-defect, and a summable revision reserve yields o(log N) finite load and compatible zero-upper-density infinite deletions.
mechanisms.kill_test: Demand a telescoping all-N inequality on RR.1 paths of arbitrary length and RR.2 future extensions; reject any potential whose decrease is only one per peeled prime or whose revisions are not summable.
